title: Sales Development Rep
mission: Turn new leads and cold contacts into booked estimate visits for Northlight's cleaning and repair crews.
outcomes_90_days: Contact every new lead within one working day, with a call and a short message
Book a steady number of estimate visits each week against a target agreed with the manager in week 2
Run a written follow up cadence so no lead goes quiet without a decision
Keep the lead sheet complete: last contact, next step and outcome for every lead
Reach out to property managers and realtors with a short, honest first message

criteria.name: Outbound experience
criteria.what_good_looks_like: The person has contacted people who did not expect to hear from them, by phone, text, email or in person, and booked something as a result.
evidence_needed: Cold calls, cold emails or door knocking with a described routine
A result such as appointments booked or customers won back
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows outbound outreach to people who did not ask to be contacted, with real examples and results

criteria.name: Written communication
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Short, clear messages that get replies. The person can show what they wrote or what it achieved.
evidence_needed: Templates, texts or emails they wrote
A reply rate or a story of a message that worked
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows the person writing clear customer messages that earned replies, with real examples

criteria.name: Follow up discipline
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Leads are followed up on a plan and on the promised date, not when the person remembers.
evidence_needed: A described cadence or reminder habit
Callbacks made on the agreed date
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows a reliable follow up routine with dates and next steps, with real examples

criteria.name: Objection handling
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Hears a no or a worry, stays calm, answers it honestly and offers a small next step.
evidence_needed: A named objection and what they said back
A script or reply they improved
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows calm, honest handling of customer objections, with real examples

criteria.name: CRM and tools
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Every contact is written down in a sheet or CRM with a next step, and the record is kept clean.
evidence_needed: A habit such as logging every call
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows careful record keeping of contacts and next steps in a CRM or sheet

criteria.name: Home service knowledge
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Understands how home repair, cleaning or property work is quoted, booked and repeated.
evidence_needed: Work with homeowners, landlords, property managers or trades
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows experience with home service customers, quotes or estimate visits

criteria.name: Coachability
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Asks for feedback, changes what they do because of it, and can say what they changed.
evidence_needed: A story of feedback received and acted on
levels: 4 did it and taught or improved it
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows the person taking feedback and changing their approach, with real examples

gates.question: Can the person legally work in the country of the role?

work_sample.title: First message to a quiet lead
work_sample.brief: A homeowner asked for a cleaning quote yesterday and has not replied. Write one short text and one short email that could get a reply. Do not invent facts about the homeowner.
work_sample.how_to_score: Score for clarity, honesty, one clear next step and a polite way to say no. Do not score spelling style or length of sentences.

interview_questions.question: Tell me about the last time you contacted someone who did not expect to hear from you. What did you say and what happened?
good_answer_signs: A real example with the opening line
A clear result or a lesson
weak_answer_signs: Only general talk about being good with people

interview_questions.question: A homeowner says to call back next Thursday. What do you do between now and Thursday?
good_answer_signs: Writes the date and time down
Calls on the day and has a plan if there is no answer
weak_answer_signs: Waits for the customer to call

interview_questions.question: A customer says your price is too high. What do you say?
good_answer_signs: Asks what they compared it to
Explains what is included and offers a smaller first step

interview_questions.question: Show me a message you wrote that got a reply. Why do you think it worked?
good_answer_signs: One clear question or next step

red_flags: Only lists skills and tools with no example of using them
Cannot describe a single follow up routine
Claims large results with no way to explain how they were reached
sourcing_channels: Local job boards the owner uses
Referrals from property managers and trades
pay_research_hint: Search the local job boards for sales development and appointment setter roles in your city and note the pay ranges shown. Ask two local business owners what they pay.
automation_note: A tool can send reminders and draft first messages. A person should make the calls, hear the tone of a worried homeowner and decide when to stop contacting someone.
